bss.topic: Revisão do 1º trimestre: território, população e economia

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Quantas são as grandes regiões do Brasil segundo a divisão oficial do IBGE?
questions.hint: Pense em Norte, Sul e as outras.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual região brasileira tem a maior área territorial?
questions.hint: É a região onde está a maior parte da Floresta Amazônica.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual região brasileira tem a maior população?
questions.hint: É a região dos estados de São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro e Minas Gerais.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Como se chama o deslocamento de pessoas do campo para as cidades?
questions.hint: A primeira palavra significa 'saída'.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: A densidade demográfica de um lugar é calculada dividindo:
questions.hint: A unidade é habitantes por km².

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Um município tem 50.000 habitantes e 250 km² de área. Qual é sua densidade demográfica, em habitantes por km²?
questions.hint: Divida a população pela área.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Na divisão em três regiões geoeconômicas, quais são os três complexos regionais do Brasil?
questions.hint: Essa divisão não segue os limites dos estados.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual é a principal fonte de geração de energia elétrica no Brasil?
questions.hint: O país tem muitos rios caudalosos com desníveis.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: A usina de Itaipu, no rio Paraná, é compartilhada entre o Brasil e qual país?
questions.hint: É um país vizinho sem saída para o mar.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Uma pirâmide etária com a base cada vez mais estreita e o topo mais largo indica que a população está:
questions.hint: Pense em quem fica na base e quem fica no topo.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Um gráfico mostra que, em 1950, a maioria dos brasileiros vivia no campo e, hoje, a grande maioria vive em cidades. Esse processo é chamado de:
questions.hint: A palavra vem de 'urbano'.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual combustível renovável é produzido em grande escala no Brasil a partir da cana-de-açúcar?
questions.hint: É usado em carros flex.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual destes é um problema ambiental ligado à construção de grandes usinas hidrelétricas?
options: Alagamento de grandes áreas de floresta e terras
Aumento da poluição do ar por fumaça
questions.answer: Alagamento de grandes áreas de floresta e terras
questions.hint: Pense no que acontece com a área do reservatório.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Em um mapa temático do Brasil, a legenda serve para:
options: explicar o significado das cores e símbolos
questions.answer: explicar o significado das cores e símbolos
questions.hint: Sem ela, as cores não teriam significado.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Explique um motivo pelo qual muitas pessoas migraram do Nordeste para o Sudeste ao longo do século XX.
questions.hint: Pense em empregos e na industrialização.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Cite uma consequência negativa da urbanização rápida nas grandes cidades brasileiras e explique por que ela acontece.
questions.hint: Pense em moradia, transporte ou saneamento.

comp.topic: Term 1 review: security, Python and data representation

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Convert the binary number 1010 to denary.
questions.hint: Use place values 8, 4, 2, 1.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Convert the denary number 13 to 4-bit binary.
questions.hint: Find which of 8, 4, 2 and 1 add up to 13.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Convert the hexadecimal digit B to denary.
questions.hint: A is 10.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Convert the denary number 47 to hexadecimal.
questions.hint: 47 = 2 × 16 + remainder.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: How many bits are in one byte?
questions.hint: A nibble is half a byte.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Why do programmers often use hexadecimal instead of binary?
options: It is shorter and easier for humans to read
questions.answer: It is shorter and easier for humans to read
questions.hint: One hex digit stands for 4 bits.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q:
What does this Python code print?
x = 5
x = x + 3
print(x * 2)
questions.hint: Trace the value of x line by line.

questions.subject: comp
questions.hint: range starts at 0 by default.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: In Python, what is the data type of the value "42" (with quotation marks)?
questions.hint: Look at the quotation marks.

questions.subject: comp
questions.hint: Is 12 greater than or equal to 13?

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: An AND gate has inputs A = 1 and B = 0. What is the output?
options: It depends on a third input
questions.hint: AND needs both inputs to be 1.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which logic gate outputs 1 when at least one input is 1?

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: An email asks you to click a link and 'confirm your password' to avoid your account being closed. What kind of attack is this most likely to be?
questions.hint: The attacker is 'fishing' for details.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Explain why a computer stores all data, such as numbers, text and images, in binary.
questions.hint: Think about the two states of an electronic switch.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Convert the binary number 110011 to denary.
questions.hint: Use place values 32, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which of these is the strongest password?
questions.hint: Think about length and variety of characters.

en.topic: Term 1 review: grammar and creative writing

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which of these is a main clause?
questions.hint: A main clause makes sense on its own.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: In the sentence 'Although it was late, Maya kept reading', which part is the subordinate clause?
questions.hint: Look for the part that cannot stand alone.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Identify the relative pronoun in this sentence: 'The boy who won the race was delighted.'
questions.hint: It introduces extra information about the boy.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence uses a semicolon correctly?
options: The sun had set; the streets grew cold.
The sun; had set and the streets grew cold.
The sun had set; and the streets.
; The sun had set, the streets grew cold.
questions.answer: The sun had set; the streets grew cold.
questions.hint: A semicolon joins two closely linked main clauses.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence uses a colon correctly?
options: She packed three things: a torch, a map and a coat.
She packed: three things a torch.
She packed three things a torch: a map.
questions.answer: She packed three things: a torch, a map and a coat.
questions.hint: A colon can introduce a list.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence uses an apostrophe correctly?
questions.hint: The apostrophe shows that the bowl belongs to the cat.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Correct the punctuation error in this sentence and write the corrected word: 'Its going to rain today.'
questions.hint: Is it a contraction or a possessive?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is a comma splice?
options: Joining two main clauses with only a comma
Using a comma in a list
Putting a comma before a quotation
questions.answer: Joining two main clauses with only a comma

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence is a comma splice?
options: I was hungry, I ate a sandwich.
I was hungry, so I ate a sandwich.
Because I was hungry, I ate a sandwich.
I was hungry; I ate a sandwich.
questions.answer: I was hungry, I ate a sandwich.
questions.hint: Which one joins two complete sentences with just a comma?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: 'Dark clouds gathered as the stranger approached the house.' Which narrative technique uses weather to reflect mood?
questions.hint: The weather mirrors the tension.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: A story suddenly jumps back to an event from the narrator's childhood. What is this technique called?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: 'Little did she know, this was the last time she would see the old key.' What technique is this?
questions.hint: It hints at what will happen later.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which opening uses a first-person narrator?
options: I had never seen the sea so still.
She had never seen the sea so still.
They had never seen the sea so still.
The sea had never been so still.
questions.answer: I had never seen the sea so still.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: A writer wants to slow down a tense moment. Which edit would help most?
options: Add precise sensory detail and short sentences
Skip ahead to the next day
Add a long list of characters' names
questions.answer: Add precise sensory detail and short sentences
questions.hint: Think about how readers feel time passing.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Rewrite this sentence to make it more vivid, using at least one technique you have studied: 'The forest was scary.'
questions.hint: Try sensory detail, a simile or personification.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Explain the difference between a main clause and a subordinate clause, using an example sentence of your own.
questions.hint: Which clause can stand alone?

en_read.topic: Term 1 review: Gothic, detective fiction and poetry

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which of these is a typical feature of Gothic fiction?
options: A gloomy, isolated setting such as a ruined castle
questions.answer: A gloomy, isolated setting such as a ruined castle

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: In detective fiction, what is a 'red herring'?
options: A misleading clue that distracts from the truth
The final solution to the crime
A clue that proves who is guilty
questions.answer: A misleading clue that distracts from the truth
questions.hint: It sends the reader in the wrong direction.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: How many lines does a sonnet have?
questions.hint: It is more than twelve.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: In many sonnets, what is the 'volta'?
options: A turn or shift in thought or argument
The first word of the poem
questions.answer: A turn or shift in thought or argument
questions.hint: The word comes from the Italian for 'turn'.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: One common sonnet form is made of three quatrains followed by what?
questions.hint: It is the final two lines.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What is the name for a line of poetry with ten syllables in an unstressed–stressed pattern?
questions.hint: 'Penta' means five.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which detail would most likely create suspense in a Gothic story?
options: A candle flickering out in an empty corridor
A cheerful picnic in the park
questions.answer: A candle flickering out in an empty corridor

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What does the term 'whodunnit' refer to?
options: A mystery story in which the reader tries to work out who committed a crime
A diary of a famous traveller
questions.answer: A mystery story in which the reader tries to work out who committed a crime

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: In the line 'The wind howled through the broken windows', which technique is used?
questions.hint: Can wind really howl?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which is the best way to support a point in an analytical paragraph?
options: Use a short, relevant quotation and explain its effect
Give your opinion with no evidence
Copy out a full page of the text
questions.answer: Use a short, relevant quotation and explain its effect

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: A detective notices mud on a visitor's boots and concludes they walked across the fields. What skill is the detective using?
questions.hint: Reaching a conclusion from evidence.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What word describes the overall feeling or atmosphere a writer creates in a text?
questions.hint: In Gothic fiction it is often dark and tense.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Why might a writer use short sentences at the climax of a story?
options: To build tension and quicken the pace
To make the text easier to skip
To slow the reader right down
questions.answer: To build tension and quicken the pace

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: In the quotation 'Her heart was a trapped bird', what is the effect of the metaphor?
options: It suggests she feels panicked and desperate to escape
It suggests she is calm and peaceful
questions.answer: It suggests she feels panicked and desperate to escape
questions.hint: Think how a trapped bird behaves.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Explain how a writer of Gothic fiction might use setting to create a sense of fear. Refer to at least two techniques.
questions.hint: Think about light, sound and isolation.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Why do you think detective stories often hold back the solution until the final chapter?
questions.hint: Think about the reader's experience.
